variant.stem_override: Vital signs: BP 158/96 mmHg, HR 84 bpm. Labs: serum creatinine 1.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9), 24-hour urine protein 4.5 g, urinalysis with microscopic hematuria and red-cell casts; anti-dsDNA antibody 480 IU/mL (markedly elevated); C3 48 mg/dL and C4 6 mg/dL (markedly low). Renal biopsy demonstrates ISN/RPS Class IV (diffuse proliferative) lupus nephritis with NIH activity index 8/24 and chronicity index 1/12 (low chronicity). These findings are from a 32-year-old woman who presents with 4 weeks of progressive lower-extremity edema and dark urine. She has a 3-year history of systemic lupus erythematosus previously managed with hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisone. She is not pregnant, has no contraindications to standard immunosuppression, and is not planning a pregnancy in the next 12 months.

All facts, values, and clinical details are identical to the base case; only their sequence has changed. The correct answer remains B because the same clinical picture — active Class IV lupus nephritis with high activity index, low chronicity, and no pregnancy plans — mandates the same induction regimen regardless of the order in which information is disclosed.
